correctness.rationale: A reflection orbits the chord vertices; fixed simplex barycentric coordinates must be equal within each orbit. Discarding orbits with internal conflicts, with edges between incompatible orbits, gives a PL inverse between the geometric fixed locus and an orbit-compatibility independence complex. The assigned source reconstructs all n(n-1)/2 chords, tests shared endpoints or interleaving, both even reflection types and all odd classes n3..12, enumerates all independent orbit sets, builds signed integer boundaries, checks boundary compositions and Smith forms. For (n,k)=(12,1), the 21 admissible orbit vertices and 125 incompatibilities produce f=(21,85,100,48,11,1) and ranks (20,61,38,10,1), all nonzero Smith factors 1, so Htilde1=Z4, Htilde2=Z. Independent exact model reproduction, mod2 full n<=12 conjugacy-class checks and independent integer Smith at n12 k1 confirmed these numbers. This finite exhaustive proof covers precisely n3..12 and all reflection conjugacy classes, not n>12 or homotopy type.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The noncrossing-forest reflection result is for edge sets forming forests and permits common endpoints; the diagonals complex of Braun–Ehrenborg admits shared endpoints and excludes boundary sides, so neither provides a dominating fixed-space theorem for pairwise vertex-disjoint chord matchings. Ambient NXM homology (Jonsson Theorem 16.9) likewise does not determine fixed-point homology.

value.rationale: Geometric fixed spaces of polygon noncrossing-matching complexes are natural equivariant topological invariants, not ordinary invariant simplices. The first mixed-degree transition at the edge-axis dodecagon and the contrast with vertex-axis fixed homology provide a sharp meaningful finite boundary that distinguishes equivariant topology from ambient homology. A complete exact integral classification through this first transition is independently useful without a general all-n theorem.

final_claim: For the geometric reflection-fixed spaces of the noncrossing matching complex of convex n-gon (all sides and chords, no shared endpoints), n3..12, the first two-degree reduced integral homology occurs at n12 for side-axis reflection τ1: Htilde1=Z4 and Htilde2=Z; the vertex-axis reflection τ0 has only Htilde1=Z3 and all smaller reflection types have only a single nonzero degree at most.
